newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX gains 2.3 percent as calm descends.
newsitem.headline: German DAX gains 2.3 percent as calm descends.

text.p: Calm descended on the German stock market on Monday, helping shares to reclaim more than half of their loses from Friday's rout and raising hopes for a resumption of the traditional pre-Christmas rally.
The 30-share DAX index ended the session up 65.28 points, or 2.3 percent, at 2,857.24 points.
The gains wiped out more than half of the DAX's four-percent slide before the weekend, which was triggered by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's warning against excessive market exuberance.
"People are starting to see that the first reaction was a bit too exaggerated," said one Frankfurt dealer.
"We are still in an uptrend," said another dealer. "The market has had the weekend to digest what happened last week and is in far calmer form."
A firm start by Bunds and the dollar's return to trade over 1.55 marks were also helping to buoy stocks although dealers said the upside was limited by residual jitters after Friday's sell-off.
Gains were spread across the board, with little major corporate news to focus interest on individual stocks. Chemical shares, Friday's biggest losers, were among the top gainers.

Utility Viag AG rose 12.50 marks to 595 marks after its packaging manufacturing unit Schmalbach Lubeca announced plans for a U.S. acquisition. Dealers said the news was mildly positive, indicating Viag's willingness to concentrate on core business areas.

Insurer Allianz AG Holding was up 37 marks at 2,822 marks, as rumours buzzed about its reported plans to sell a 15 percent stake in BHF Bank. The group has denied it has concrete plans to do so but has not ruled out the prospect completely.
"Something is going to happen there, we are sure of that," said a Frankfurt trader.
